outputs.L1: We prove that the limiting hypersurfaces of convergent curvature flows are stable when the initial velocity has a weak sign, and we survey the relevant existence and regularity results.
outputs.L2: We establish the stability of limiting hypersurfaces arising from convergent curvature flows when the initial velocity is weakly one-signed, and we review the relevant existence and regularity results.
outputs.L3: This work investigates curvature flows that converge to limiting hypersurfaces. Its main result establishes the stability of these limit hypersurfaces under the assumption that the initial velocity has a weak sign, meaning that it is consistently nonnegative or nonpositive, possibly vanishing at some points. In addition to proving this stability result, the work reviews the existence and regularity theory relevant to the curvature flows under consideration, providing the analytical framework needed to understand their convergence and the properties of the resulting hypersurfaces.
outputs.L4:
This work investigates curvature-driven evolutions of hypersurfaces that converge as time tends to infinity. The analysis begins with initial data whose associated normal velocity satisfies only a weak sign condition, allowing the velocity to vanish and avoiding the need for strict mean-convexity or strict monotonicity. Within this setting, the paper reviews the existence, uniqueness, and regularity results needed to ensure that the flow is well defined and remains sufficiently controlled throughout its evolution. Particular attention is given to the preservation of the weak sign condition and to the estimates required to pass to the limit.

Assuming that the evolving hypersurfaces converge to a limiting hypersurface, the work then studies the linearized geometric operator at that limit. By relating the preserved sign of the velocity to the corresponding linearized equation, it shows that the principal eigenvalue has the appropriate sign. This yields stability of the limiting hypersurface under normal variations. Consequently, a weak one-sided condition on the initial motion provides a practical criterion for determining the long-term behavior of the flow: whenever such a flow exists, remains regular, and converges, its limit must be stable. The result brings together standard existence and regularity theory with a direct stability argument and applies broadly to convergent curvature flows in geometric analysis.
outputs.L5: “We prove that” is a common phrase in mathematical and scientific writing. It introduces a claim that will be established through logical reasoning, evidence, or formal calculations. A complete proof typically begins with known assumptions, applies valid definitions and previously established results, and proceeds step by step until the desired conclusion follows. Every argument must be clear and justified so that readers can verify the result independently. Thus, when we say, “We prove that,” we are not merely stating that something is true—we are promising a rigorous demonstration of why it must be true.

counterfactuals.prompt: Generate an abstract for a research note about stable limiting hypersurfaces in curvature flows with weakly signed initial velocity.
counterfactuals.output: We study the long-time behavior of curvature flows whose initial normal velocity has a weak sign, allowing degeneracy along nontrivial subsets of the initial hypersurface. Under natural geometric and compactness assumptions, we show that the evolving hypersurfaces become strictly monotone for positive times and converge, after an appropriate parametrization, to a stationary limiting hypersurface. The limit is stable with respect to the linearized curvature operator and is independent of the choice of regularization used to remove the initial degeneracy. Our argument combines a strong maximum principle for the velocity equation, barrier constructions, monotonicity estimates, and elliptic compactness. We also discuss the extent to which convergence remains smooth near the zero-velocity set and give examples illustrating the necessity of the weak sign and stability hypotheses. These results provide a link between one-sided dynamical evolution and variational stability in degenerate curvature-flow settings.
counterfactuals.label: cf_3
